Currently, there are seven inhabited permanent dwellings and seven mobile homes within the boundaries of Tracts II and III. As mining progresses, it will be necessary for some or all of these families to relocate. Ranching families should be able to acquire new properties using money gained from land sales as some have done, but leaving family ranches and beginning operation in new locations will be at least temporarily disruptive to those involved.
Risk of Accidents
Industry Related - The risk of fatal and disabling accidents to the employees in any industrial operation depends on many factors in addition to the physical hazards of the work. The experience, motivation and training of employees, as well as management's commitment to safety, can have a great effect on accident rates. Underground coal mining is a much more hazardous occupation than surface coal mining in terms of fatalities and disabling accidents. The risks involved in working in a surface coal mine are much smaller and are comparable to risks in the construction industries.
